newsitem.title: USA: New York Bagel fares well after IPO.
newsitem.headline: New York Bagel fares well after IPO.

text.p: Shares of New York Bagel Enterprises Inc rose in early trading on Tuesday after the company's initial public offering.

The shares rose to 10-1/2, up from their IPO price of $9 a share. The company offered two million shares, which had been estimated to price in a range of $9 to $11. That price range had been dropped a notch from an original estimated pricing of $10 to $12 a share.
Of the shares sold in the IPO, New York Bagel offered 1.8 million shares and selling shareholders offered 200,000.
The company, which is based in Witchita, Kansas, owns and franchises over 50 New York Bagel restaurants in 16 states and has posted profits for the past three years.
Rauscher Pierce Refsnes is the lead underwriter of the offering. J.C. Bradford & Co was also an underwriter.
The company said it plans to use proceeds to repay debt, finance the development of company owned restaurants, possible acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
